name: Riwaq Water
summary: A compact mosque meets a single broad water ribbon at its foundation, recalling the stillness of an ablution courtyard.
why: The square minaret is physically joined to the domed hall. A water ribbon takes over the shared foundation, touching every pier rather than appearing as a separate decorative object. Its shallow curve offsets the firm architectural rhythm.
risk: The water can read as a soft ground line at very small sizes. It is a symbolic courtyard, not a literal architectural plan.

palette.name: RIWAQ WATER / SLATE + IVORY + SEA GLASS

reasonToChoose: You want the mosque to feel peaceful through an integrated water motif.
